chapter_seo_title: Dao Gui Yi Xian Ch. 563: The Dice’s Final Play — A Dynasty Overturned With One Confession
chapter_meta_description: The Dice, nailed to the ground, reveals his ultimate scheme: Emperor Ji Lin is actually a woman. The Dragon Vein of Great Liang faces its gravest threat yet.
og_title: “He’s Actually a Woman” — The Dice’s Final Confession Rocks Great Liang
og_description: Pinned down by six Military generals, the Dice drops the dynastic bomb: Ji Lin’s manhood was a Zuowandao deception. A stone-woman now sits on the Dragon Throne.
twitter_title: The Dice’s Final Laugh: “The Emperor Is a Woman”
twitter_description: Even half-dead, the Dice wins. The Great Liang Dragon Vein is broken at the root—and Li Huowang just realized he helped make it happen.

lore_anchors.definition: A being or sect that cannot be named by mortal mouths or recorded in writing; born from the void, it can only be glimpsed at the edges of death or extreme grief.
In this novel’s lore, the Wu are ancient beings who farmed humans as livestock; the ancestors of humanity escaped them and used the stolen Mandate to create their own sheltered world.
A traditional Chinese term for a woman with vaginal agenesis; in this novel, it is weaponized as a dynastic curse that severs the Dragon Vein.
The subterranean energy channel that sustains a dynasty’s legitimacy in Chinese geomancy; the Zuowandao cannot move it, but they can destroy the vessel meant to inherit it.
A practitioner of the martial path, whose murderous aura is so dense it can cause hallucinations in weaker cultivators.
A slow, agonizing execution method by slicing; Li Huowang threatens the hallucinatory Zuowandao with it.
Huangfu Tiangang’s personal weapon; likely tied to celestial or astrological power.
